findings.issue_text: [High/bug] src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:25 — `to_dict()` returns a raw `datetime` from `asdict`, making Celery task kwargs non-JSON-serializable and potentially failing outbound sync enqueueing.

[Medium/bug] src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:408 — `assignment_source` is added to `sync_status_outbound`, but status task/callers do not propagate it into `should_sync`, so status syncs can echo back to their originating integration.

[Low/data] src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:17 — `timezone.now()` is evaluated at module import time, causing every `AssignmentSource` in the process to receive the same stale `queued` timestamp.

goldens.comment: The AssignmentSource dataclass uses queued: datetime = timezone.now() as a default field value, which evaluates timezone.now() once at class definition time and shares that single datetime instance across all objects.
The method name has a typo: test_from_dict_inalid_data should be test_from_dict_invalid_data.
Method name says 'empty_array' but tests empty dict - consider renaming to 'test_from_dict_empty_dict' for clarity.
to_dict() returns a datetime for queued; if this dict is passed in task kwargs (e.g., via apply_async), JSON serialization may fail depending on the serializer, which can cause enqueue errors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:408 — `assignment_source` is added to `sync_status_outbound`, but status task/callers do not propagate it into `should_sync`, so status syncs can echo back to their originating integration.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is accurate. Looking at the diff, `sync_status_outbound` in the abstract method signature (lines 408-417) now accepts `assignment_source: AssignmentSource | None = None`, but there's no corresponding update to any status sync task or caller to pass this parameter through to `should_sync()`. The `should_sync` method was updated to accept `sync_source` parameter and check for cycle prevention (lines 382-393), but this protection only works if callers actually pass the source. The diff shows `sync_assignee_outbound` task was updated to pass `parsed_assignment_source` to `should_sync`, but there's no equivalent update shown for status sync tasks. This means status syncs could still echo back to their originating integration, creating sync cycles.
